partners.mechanism_chain: DSPP (HGNC:2770) —DISRUPTS→ Deafness, autosomal dominant 39 (HP:0000365); DSPP (HGNC:2770) —DISRUPTS→ Dentinogenesis imperfecta 1 (HP:0000301); HSPG2 (HGNC:4932) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1 (HP:0000367). Mutations in DSPP disrupt the formation of dentin and enamel, leading to dentinogenesis imperfecta and contributing to hearing loss. Mutations in HSPG2 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, which is critical for skeletal and connective tissue development, manifesting as Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1. While DSPP's primary role is in dentin and enamel, and HSPG2 in broader connective tissues, both genes are integral to extracellular matrix homeostasis. Dysfunction in these fundamental ECM processes can lead to convergent phenotypic effects, particularly in tissues reliant on specific ECM compositions like the inner ear and bone.
